issues.description: The problem statement's textual task list refers to attributes named 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' while the UML diagram (and the provided solution) use 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'. This name discrepancy in the problem description may confuse students about the exact attribute names they should implement and the corresponding getter/setter names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute names consistent in the problem statement: update the textual task list to use 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' to match the UML and solution (or alternatively, change the UML and solution to use 'inscribedStudents'/'guestStudents'). Ensure the examples and test descriptions consistently use the same exact names so students know which getters/setters to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement (line listing the required attributes) refers to the student-count attributes as 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents', while the UML diagram and the solution implementation use 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual attributes can cause students to choose the shorter names in their implementation and then be unable to map to the UML/tests that expect the 'numberOf...' prefixed identifiers.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute names consistent across all artifacts. Update problem_statement.md to list 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (matching the UML and solution), or alternatively change the UML and solution to use 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' everywhere. Prefer keeping 'numberOf...' prefixes to match the getters/tests (e.g., getNumberOfInscribedStudents).
